correctness.rationale: The proof is an exhaustive necessary-and-sufficient case split on spine inclusion and page states. Each matching obstruction is local and explicit: singleton x-pages can use only spine a and singleton y-pages only spine b; the one-sided singleton case with both spines strands the mate of any full page used by the remaining spine. The resulting disjoint classes give the displayed polynomial. A direct brute-force checker reconstructs domination and perfect matching and matches the formula through n=8; that finite check is not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Square books are the natural star-by-edge Cartesian products appearing directly in the graph-product setting for paired domination. The claim gives a complete set classification and every polynomial coefficient, exposing how a global perfect-matching constraint collapses to four page-state patterns. This strictly refines the elementary scalar minimum and supplies exact total and minimum-set counts.
